name: OpenCode
run-name: "OpenCode #${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}${{ github.event.issue.title && format(' — {0}', github.event.issue.title) || '' }}"

on:
  issues:
    types: [opened]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      issue_number:
        description: Existing issue to run
        required: true
        type: string

permissions: {}

concurrency:
  group: opencode-issue-${{ github.repository }}-${{ github.event.issue.number || inputs.issue_number }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  prepare:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' || (github.event.action == 'opened' && contains(github.event.issue.labels.*.name, 'OpenCode'))
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-prepare.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2

  opencode:
    needs: prepare
    if: needs.prepare.outputs.approved == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
      actions: read
      pull-requests: write
    uses: denaidark/OhMyGithub/.github/workflows/opencode-reusable.yml@3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
    with:
      runtime_ref: 3b460fef6b0cbee61ae301726c8a54b00b73bfd2
      issue_number: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_number }}
      request: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.request }}
      issue_title: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.issue_title }}
      labels_json: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.labels_json }}
      sender: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.sender }}
      target_ref: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_ref }}
      target_sha: ${{ needs.prepare.outputs.target_sha }}
    secrets:
      OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
      OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_AUTH_JSON }}

# OMG (Oh My GitHub) agent instructions

Do not implement, suggest, report, or propose security issues unless the user explicitly asks for a security review.
Inspect the OpenCode implementation at `/Users/igor/Documents/ChatGPT/opencode` and [anomalyco/opencode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode) for related requests.

## Wiki index

- [OpenCode workflow](wiki/opencode.md)
- [Test OpenCode execution](wiki/opencode-v2-experiment.md)
- [Oh My Github App](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/oh-my-github-app.md)
- [Temporary Mac SSH access](wiki/access.md)
- [Testing and verification](wiki/testing.md)
- [OmGithub publishing](https://github.com/denaidark/omsite/blob/main/wiki/omgithub.md)


## Main project file

The main project file is [.github/workflows/opencode.yml](.github/workflows/opencode.yml).

Keep the local [game issue E2E skill](.agents/skills/game-issue-e2e/SKILL.md)
aligned with this workflow. Create an issue with `OpenCode` and only user-requested mode labels already attached, to start the native `issues.opened` listener. Wait only for the
initial OpenCode session link during E2E kickoff. Install the listener on the
default branch before requesting execution. Validate author access and freeze
the request inside Actions before starting the reusable execution job.
Set repository variable `OPENCODE_ACCESS=everyone` to accept any issue author
for labeled issues. Keep the App as a setup
helper. Use Actions concurrency to serialize each issue.
Store `branch` in an `omgithub-request:v1` JSON HTML comment to select the
project checkout, result base, and workflow. Let default-branch preparation
dispatch the selected branch. Run preparation and OpenCode in that branch run.

## Shell timing

When writing shell scripts,
always add explicit per-command execution-time measurements between commands.
Use `/usr/bin/time -p` or a small timing helper around each meaningful command;
the outer command duration is not sufficient because it hides which step is
slow or hung. Use `/usr/bin/time` only in scripts; do not invoke it directly in
interactive shell commands.

## Ideas

Store durable implementation ideas as individual Markdown files under
`./ideas/`, using descriptive kebab-case filenames such as
`ideas/opencode-oauth-env-auth.md`.




## Links in handoffs

When a relevant URL or stable identifier exists, include a clickable Markdown
link in the user-facing response. Link GitHub issues, Actions runs, pull
requests, commits, releases, public app URLs, and Codex tasks/threads rather
than reporting only their numbers or plain text. For Codex tasks/threads, use
the `codex://threads/<thread-id>` URL format.

When mentioning a commit, append its relative age in hours or days.

## OpenCode GitHub Actions

To execute an issue, create it with `OpenCode` and only mode labels explicitly requested by the user.
Check for a native `issues` run and successful preparation.
The workflow starts a temporary AgentsWeb SSH session,
verifies it, runs OpenCode, and cleans up the SSH session afterward.

When monitoring a triggered run, use `gh run watch <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --exit-status` for overall job status.
Do not use `gh run view --log` to read logs from a running task: GitHub reports that
logs are unavailable until completion. Use `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>`
for the live Actions log over SSH. Do not use tight `for` loops around `gh run list`,
which needlessly consume GitHub API rate limit.

Free OpenCode models are limited per egress IP, not per account.
Treat a local `FreeUsageLimitError` 429 as local only.
Read the runner's own `Selected model` and provider errors before blaming quota.
Use `retryAfterMs` as the reset bound.
Run repeated V2 tests with a connected provider; do not spend the free allowance on retries.

Interrupting a V2 turn before the assistant message projects leaves no stopped message to save.
Wait for that assistant message before requiring the interrupted idle marker.

To connect to an issue's live worker, find its run ID with
`gh run list --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub --workflow opencode.yml --status in_progress`,
then run `bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>` to discover the host and port and SSH
with `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb` as shown by the helper.

When the user asks to check a live OpenCode workflow, always pull the runner logs
over SSH first, using `scripts/ssh-run-log.sh` or a targeted SSH read from the
same runner. Base the answer on those logs before discussing whether an action
is confirmed; do not lead with a generic inability-to-confirm statement when
live log evidence can be collected.

For real-time inspection from a live temporary SSH session, use the helper:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id>
```

The helper discovers the temporary SSH command from the triggering issue or pull
request, then follows the freshest `_diag/pages` log. The runner uploads chunks from
`_diag/blocks` to GitHub. Do not print environment files, tokens, or private keys while
inspecting the runner.

## Mac SSH access

The Mac private key stays at `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`. Its public key is
stored in the repository Actions secret `AGENTSWEB_SSH_PUBLIC_KEY`. The issue
commented by the workflow contains a directly usable command such as:

```sh
ssh -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

The command works only while the corresponding Actions job is running.

## Connecting to a live OpenCode worker

Use the repository helper to discover the worker host and port from the broker
or issue comment. It uses the persistent local key `~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb`:

```sh
bash scripts/ssh-run-log.sh <run-id> --repo denaidark/OhMyGithub
```

For an interactive shell, reuse the host and port printed by the helper and
use the same key:

```sh
ssh -tt -o StrictHostKeyChecking=no \
  -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
  -i ~/.ssh/aiplay-agentsweb \
  -p <port> runner@<run-name>.agentsweb.space
```

Do not substitute the generated runner key under `sshworker/outputs/keys/`; it
can produce a misleading `Permission denied (publickey)` result. Temporary
worker SSH access ends when the Actions job and session are cleaned up. Never
print secrets while inspecting a worker.

content.text:
So the setup expects an index.html (or vite project). We can build a static HTML/CSS/JS game. Need to be visually beautiful. Let's plan a game.

Concept: "Slime & Seek" — a hide-and-seek game where you play a slime that can reshape and recolor to blend into terrain. The seeker (a lantern-eyed warden) patrols and scans.

Gameplay design:
- Top-down 2.5D or side view? Terrain matching suggests top-down with patterned terrain zones. Could do a 3D-ish arena using Three.js, or 2D canvas with beautiful art.

Given quality and time, a 2D canvas game with rich procedural rendering can look great and be reliable. But Three.js would allow "shape shifting" visual 3D slime. Hmm. The requirements are vague; impressive visual demo will help. A polished 2D game with fluid slime physics, terrains with distinct colors/textures, camouflage mechanic based on color proximity + shape matching, seeker AI with vision cone, levels, UI, audio (WebAudio synthesized), mobile support.

Alternatively, a 3D arena top-down with Three.js, slime blob with vertex deformation, terrain patches (moss, stone, sand, water, lava), shape selector (blob, puddle, pillar, spike, boulder), color picker. Seeker patrols with flashlight. This could look gorgeous with soft shadows, fog, particles. Three.js from CDN? Network may be unavailable at runtime in preview, and relying on CDN is risky. Could vendor three.js via npm and use vite. But default-start supports vite and installs. Could use npm package three + vite. That's a possibility but heavy. Let's check network/npm availability.

We can also do raw WebGL/canvas. A carefully crafted 2D canvas scene with parallax, fog, glow, procedural textures can look very polished and runs everywhere. I think a web game best played with mouse/touch and keyboard.

Let me settle on a design:

**Slime & Seek** — top-down hide-and-seek in a "Mosslight Grove" arena. You are a slime (playable blob) that must survive 3 rounds / fill "hide meter". A seeker with a vision cone patrols. You score by blending:
- **Hue match**: choose color from palette or fine-tune to match the ground patch under you.
- **Shape match**: cycle between shapes (blob, puddle, tuft, rock, log?) that correspond to terrain features. Shape affects movement speed and camouflage.
- Camouflage percentage computed from color distance + shape-terrain match + motion + light.

// Start gameplay once without guessing between multiple controls or following links.
export async function startForCapture(page, { enabled = true, selector = '', timeout = 3000 } = {}) {
  if (!enabled) return { clicked: false, reason: 'disabled' }
  const candidate = selector
    ? page.locator(selector)
    : page.locator('button, input[type="button"], input[type="submit"], [role="button"]')
  const deadline = Date.now() + timeout
  do {
    const matches = []
    for (const control of await candidate.all()) {
      if (!await control.isVisible() || !await control.isEnabled()) continue

        const label = element.getAttribute('aria-label') || element.value || element.textContent || ''
        return /^(?:start|play)(?:\s+(?:game|now))?$/i.test(label.trim())
      }, Boolean(selector))
      if (eligible) matches.push(control)
    }
    if (matches.length > 1) return { clicked: false, reason: 'ambiguous' }
    if (matches.length === 1) {
      try { await matches[0].click({ trial: true, timeout: 2000 }) }
      catch (error) {
        if (error.name === 'TimeoutError') return { clicked: false, reason: 'not-actionable' }
        throw error
      }
      await matches[0].click({ timeout: 2000, noWaitAfter: true })
      return { clicked: true }
    }
    if (Date.now() >= deadline) break
    await page.waitForTimeout(Math.min(200, Math.max(0, deadline - Date.now())))
  } while (Date.now() <= deadline)
  return { clicked: false, reason: 'not-found' }
}
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Start the saved project and publish readiness only after both HTTP checks pass.
set -euo pipefail
cd "${PROJECT_DIR:?}"
: "${OPENCODE_WEB_DIR:?}" "${APP_URL:?}"
PORT="${APP_PORT:-3000}"
export PORT
startup_timeout="${STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS:-600}"
[[ "$startup_timeout" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]] || { echo 'STARTUP_TIMEOUT_SECONDS must be a positive integer.' >&2; exit 1; }
/usr/bin/time -p test -f start.sh
/usr/bin/time -p bash -n start.sh
current_commit="${CHECKPOINT_COMMIT:-}"
previous_commit=""
[[ ! -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit" ]] || previous_commit="$(/usr/bin/time -p cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit")"
# Reuse an in-flight build for this checkpoint when a readiness retry returns.
starting=false
if [[ -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit" ]] && [[ "$(/usr/bin/time -p cat "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit")" == "$current_commit" ]] && /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null; then
  starting=true
fi
if [[ "${RESTART_APP:-false}" == true ]] || { [[ "$starting" == false ]] && { [[ -n "$current_commit" && "$previous_commit" != "$current_commit" ]] || ! /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 3 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" >/dev/null; }; }; then
  /usr/bin/time -p rm -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/ready-preview-url"
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux kill-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || true
  /usr/bin/time -p node "${RUNTIME_DIR:?}/scripts/reclaim-preview-port.mjs"
  /usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$current_commit" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit"
  # Pass paths through tmux's environment; keep the script in the foreground.
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux new-session -d -s app-server -c "$PROJECT_DIR" \
    -e "RUNTIME_DIR=${RUNTIME_DIR:?}" -e "OPENCODE_WEB_DIR=$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR" -e "PORT=$PORT" -e "STARTUP_LOG=$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/app.log" \
    'bash start.sh > "$STARTUP_LOG" 2>&1'
fi
ready=false
for ((attempt=0; attempt<(startup_timeout + 1) / 2; attempt++)); do
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || { echo 'Startup process exited. Inspect app.log.' >&2; exit 1; }
  if /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 3 "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/" >/dev/null; then
    ready=true
    break
  fi
  /usr/bin/time -p tmux has-session -t app-server 2>/dev/null || { echo 'Startup process exited. Inspect app.log.' >&2; exit 1; }
  /usr/bin/time -p sleep 2
done
[[ "$ready" == true ]] || { echo "Local startup failed after ${startup_timeout}s. Inspect app.log." >&2; exit 75; }
/usr/bin/time -p rm -f "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/starting-commit"
# Local readiness is independent of a temporary public tunnel failure.
/usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$current_commit" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/served-commit"
for ((attempt=0; attempt<12; attempt++)); do
  status="$(/usr/bin/time -p curl --silent --show-error --location --max-time 10 --output "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/public-readiness.log" --write-out '%{http_code}' "$APP_URL")" || status=000
  if [[ "$status" == 2* ]]; then
    /usr/bin/time -p /usr/bin/printf '%s' "$APP_URL" > "$OPENCODE_WEB_DIR/ready-preview-url"
    if [[ -n "${OPENCODE_CONTROL_PORT:-}" ]]; then
      /usr/bin/time -p curl --fail --silent --max-time 5 "http://127.0.0.1:$OPENCODE_CONTROL_PORT/omgithub/heartbeat" >/dev/null || true
    fi
    echo 'Local and public preview are ready.'
    exit 0
  fi
  if [[ "$status" == 4* && "$status" != 408 && "$status" != 429 ]]; then
    echo "Public preview rejected the request (HTTP $status). Inspect public-readiness.log." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
  /usr/bin/time -p sleep 2
done
echo 'Public preview did not become ready.' >&2
exit 75

disc = b*b-c
if disc>=0: t = -b - sqrt(disc); if t>0 return t
```

content.text:
The user has now clarified a lot, changing design significantly. They want:
- Play UI with directional key or joystick.
- A button to switch between disguise mode and movement mode.
- A key with the ability to climb walls.
- In disguise mode, selecting a shape changes the slime shape according to the shape applied by touching it (i.e., touch/scan an object to copy its shape).
- A color palette displayed, and ability to paint the slime similarly to the surrounding background.
- Play style divided into a hidden slime team and tagger team that finds and hunts the slime (multiplayer-ish/asymmetric).
- Similar to game "Metcha Chameleon" on Steam, if similar games exist.

We need to adjust our design accordingly. Let me research "Metcha Chameleon" to understand gameplay. Use web search/fetch.

Key points:
- Asymmetric hide-and-seek: chameleons hide by changing color/shape, seekers hunt.
- In Metcha Chameleon, it's an online multiplayer game? Let's search.

We may need to implement a single-player game that simulates both teams, or local multiplayer? The user says "The play style should be divided into a hidden slime team and a tagger team that finds and hunts such slime." Could mean game modes: player can choose hider (slime) or seeker (tagger). We should support single-player against AI for both roles, maybe hot-seat local? Let's research first.

Also "a key with the ability to climb walls" — in a top-down game, walls/3D climbing is awkward. Metcha Chameleon is likely 3D third-person, where players climb walls and disguise as objects. We may need to pivot to a 3D game with Three.js? Let's inspect the reference.

Search web.

## About This Game

Paint your own body! Blend in like a chameleon in this hide-and-seek game!

## **yeah! Mechcha "Hide and Seek"**

The rules are simple. Split into the Seeker team and the Hider team to play hide-and-seek. The Seekers win if they find everyone within the time limit.

## **yeah! Mechcha "Paint"**

The way you hide is a bit special. Paint your pure white body to blend into the stage. Just like a chameleon. The hiding spot, the pose, and above all, your artistic skills are the key! Deceive the Seekers' eyes with a mimicry that would even surprise a chameleon.

## **yeah! Mechcha "Matching"**

Of course you can play with friends, but you can also play with people you don't know. (If you create a server that is not set to private, anyone can join freely.) Game streamers can easily host viewer participation games. The maximum number of players depends on the host's network environment. (2–10 players recommended. ## Objective
- Build a playable hide-and-seek browser game where the player controls a slime that changes shape and color to match terrain and hide.

## Requirements
- Character is a slime.
- Player can modify its shape and color to blend into terrain and hide.
- No other explicit mechanics, platform, or visual constraints were given.

## Decisions
- Build a polished, self-contained static HTML/CSS/JS game with ES modules and Canvas 2D; no build step or external runtime dependencies.
- Game concept: **Slime & Seek** in a moonlit grove; collect three moon motes while avoiding a lantern-wielding seeker.
- Core loop: move onto one of six terrain zones, match its color and required shape, stand still to build camouflage, lure the mote, avoid the seeker's vision cone.
- Mechanics: 4 shapes (Pool, Mound, Shard, Tuft), 8-color palette, camo from color match + shape match + stillness, 3 hearts, dash cooldown, line-of-sight blocked by boulders, escalating seeker per night.
- UX: title, how-to/field guide, HUD with blend meter/compass/hearts/score, pause, win/lose results, mobile joystick/touch controls, procedural WebAudio ambience/SFX.
- Vendored local Fraunces and Outfit WOFF2 fonts plus OFL licenses.
- Planned file structure: `index.html`, `styles.css`, `src/{main,game,ui,render,world,audio,utils}.js`, `assets/fonts/`.

## Work State
### Completed
- Inspected empty playground and runtime expectations; static `index.html` is supported.
- Downloaded and vendored fonts/licences into `assets/fonts/`.
- Implemented `src/utils.js` with math, color, RNG, path, and formatting helpers.
- Implemented `src/world.js` with world bounds, 6 zones, 8-color palette, 4 shapes, boulders, seeker patrol points, generated decorative data, and LOS/collision helpers.

### Active
- Implementing remaining modules: `audio.js`, `render.js`, `game.js`, `ui.js`, `main.js`, then `index.html` and `styles.css`.
- After implementation: run server and verify with Playwright screenshots across desktop and mobile, then iterate on visuals and gameplay.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Create `src/audio.js` with procedural ambient loop and SFX (morph, select, dash, hidden, collect, alert, caught, win).
2. Create `src/render.js`: camera follow/zoom, painterly ground and zone patterns, y-sorted entities, boulders/trees/decor, slime morph rendering, seeker with clipped vision cone, motes, particles, fireflies, fog, glow sprites.
3. Create `src/game.js`: state machine, input (keyboard/touch joystick), camo/detection/chase/catch logic, mote spawning and collection, score, hearts, night escalation.
4. Create `src/ui.js`, `src/main.js`, `index.html`, `styles.css` matching the planned IDs/UI screens.
5. Serve on port 3002 and verify title, gameplay, help, results, mobile portrait/landscape with `playwright-cli`; inspect screenshots and iterate.

- `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/src/world.js`: completed terrain/game-world data and helpers; exports `WORLD`, `ZONES`, `COLORS`, `SHAPES`, `OBSTACLES`, `PATROL`, `zoneAt`, `rayCast`, `segmentBlocked`, `collideObstacles`, `lineOfSight`, `safeSpotAround`, etc.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.
- Follow explicit device and control requirements in the user request.

## Objective
- Build a polished, playable browser hide-and-seek game inspired by *MECCHA CHAMELEON*, where a slime player mimics terrain shapes/colors, paints its body, climbs walls, and evades a lantern-wielding seeker; support both slime-hider and warden-seeker roles.

## Requirements
- Play UI must include directional keys/joystick, a move/disguise mode toggle, and a climb-wall action.
- In disguise mode, touching terrain/objects changes the slime shape, a color palette appears, and the player can paint the slime to match the surrounding ground.
- Gameplay is split into a hidden slime team and a tagger/seeker team.
- Resemble *MECCHA CHAMELEON*: pose/shape matching, body painting, line-of-sight hiding, team hide-and-seek.
- Must work on desktop and mobile with usable touch controls and safe-area-aware layout.
- Self-contained static HTML/CSS/JS with local fonts and no external runtime assets/build step.

## Decisions
- Implemented as a static Canvas 2D game titled **Slime & Seek**, served from `index.html`.
- Two roles: Slime team (survive 1:40, paint/shape/blend) and Warden (sweep lantern, pulse, tag all 5 AI slimes).
- Hider tools: four movement plus disguise mode toggle (`Q`), touch/`E` copy shapes, paint palette + direct painting on a slime canvas, `F`/Match Ground sampling, `Space` climb/cling, `Shift` dash.
- Seeker tools: mouse or movement-direction aiming, fog-of-war vision cone, `E` lantern pulse/heartbeat reveal, `Space`/click tag.
- Blend formula combines paint color, paint texture, shape match, and stillness; movement/dashing lowers camouflage.
- Seeker detection uses vision cone, line-of-sight, camouflage, movement noise, suspicion buildup, chase/search/patrol states, with a short start grace period.
- World includes 6 terrain zones, 7 scannable prop types/landmarks, boulders and tall climbable standing stones, procedural decorations, fireflies, particles, glow effects, and painterly lighting.
- Performance optimization added: baked static world background cache, cached entity sprites for trees/props/rocks/decor, viewport sub-rect drawing, and lightweight animated zone shimmer overlay.
- Mobile zoom was increased (`compact` branch targeting ~0.72 at 390×844) so slimes remain readable and the camera follows instead of showing the whole world.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented all modules: `src/utils.js`, `src/world.js`, `src/slime.js`, `src/paint.js`, `src/audio.js`, `src/render.js`, `src/game.js`, `src/ui.js`, `src/main.js`.
- Implemented `index.html` with title, role selection, one exact `Play` button, HUD, disguise tray, seeker panel, joystick, guide, pause, and results overlays.
- Implemented `styles.css` with vendored Fraunces/Outfit fonts, botanical field-guide styling, responsive desktop/mobile layouts.
- Added `assets/favicon.svg` and vendored fonts/licenses.
- Verified JS syntax with `node --check`.
- Served game on port 3002 in tmux session `slime`.
- Verified desktop title, hider gameplay, disguise panel, results, mobile title, and mobile gameplay with Playwright screenshots.
- Fixed renderer syntax error (`const ctx` redeclaration in `drawFog`).
- Fixed immediate seeker spawn/catch by moving seeker to `(1390, 905)`, adding a 3.4s grace period, slowing suspicion buildup, freezing actors during countdown, and reducing countdown to 0.55s.
- Performance improved from ~2 fps to roughly environment baseline (~5–8 fps on SwiftShader; blank page was ~8 fps).
- Screenshot timeouts at 1440×900 resolved after caching.

### Active
- Final visual and gameplay verification, especially mobile disguise tray, joystick interaction, seeker role, climb action, pause/results, and mode toggle.
- Check for any remaining layout polish or gameplay balance issues after the latest mobile-zoom change.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Screenshot mobile disguise mode by tapping/pressing `Q`; verify paint canvas, palette, shape chips, and action buttons fit without overflow.
2. Test seeker role via results “Try the other side” or `game.startMatch('seeker')`; verify fog, aim, lantern pulse, tag action, HUD, and win/lose flow.
3. Test climb near a standing stone/boulder with `Space`, verify camera/render behavior and drop action.
